To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stable isotope composition of the solid residues of wines is a useful indicator for the vine water status and the N dynamics in vineyard soils.

the carbon isotope ratios in dried wines are good proxies for the soil water status, and the nitrogen isotope ratios and the carbon/nitrogen ratios in dried wines provide a reliable record of the soil nitrogen dynamics.

The carbon and nitrogen isotope composition of dried wines reflects the plant water status (and thus the soil water availability) and the origin of nitrogen supplied to the fruit (grape), respectively".
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of the stable isotope composition (δ13C, δ15N) of the solid residue obtained by freeze-dried wine as a tool to trace back the climatic conditions of the growing season of the grapevine.

the development of an innovative tool for tracing back climate-induced changes in soil water availability and soil water dynamics in the vineyard, which are the most important factors affecting grapevine physiology and wine quality.
the use of wine as an archive of environmental conditions and the dynamics of soil water availability in the vineyard.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the carbon and nitrogen isotopic composition of dried wines is a reliable indicator to trace back soil water availability in the vineyard and to assess the soil and the N dynamics in vineyards.
the carbon isotope ratio of wine solid residues (C/NWSRs) is a reliable proxy for the soil water regime in the vineyard.

the stable isotope composition of the solid residue of wines (i.e., C/NWSR, C/NWSR/δ15NWSR and δ13CWSRs) is a reliable indicator for the origin of the water and nutrients used in the production of wine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by using stable isotope compositions of dried wines, we can trace back the soil and plant water status and the N dynamics in soil-plant systems.

the stable isotope composition (δ13C, δ15N) of the solid residue of wine can be used as an indicator of soil water availability, and of the nitrogen origin in the plant's fruit, and therefore, of the nitrogen cycling in the soil-water system.
, for the studied grapevine varieties, wine solid residues are reliable tracers of soil and plant water status and N dynamics in the vineyard.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the stable isotope composition (δ13CWSR) of wine solid residues provides an accurate and reliable proxy of soil water availability in the vineyard, and can be used to track back local climatic changes.

the carbon and nitrogen contents of dried wines can be used to reconstruct past climate conditions in the vineyards and to monitor the impact of climate change on the vineyard water status and N dynamics.
wine can be used as a proxy to trace back changes in the vineyard water regime, which can be used to reconstruct past climates.
